title: SoftFall resume safeguard and tenant gradual thaw hotfix
author: Marco Bellini
description:
Summary: This hotfix introduces a lightweight 'SoftFall' resume safeguard and a tenant 'gradual thaw' path to prevent immediate large-scale reopen storms after circuit-driven quarantines. Motivation: We observed a post-quarantine surge where many tenants attempted immediate retries on reconnect, triggering KV pressure and causing secondary SLO violations. The patch adds an orchestrated, telemetry-driven slow-resume path that staggers tenant reconnect attempts and trims connection pacing on noisy clients.

What this PR implements (single continuous description): Adds a controller that tracks ephemeral quarantine windows and assigns a small, sliding thaw token budget to each tenant to pace resume attempts; introduces a soft resume proxy that enforces a per-tenant expedite flag and connection pace trimming (reduces permitted concurrent inflight) when KV pressure or tail-latency regressions are detected; records a circuit snapshot token on quarantine events to aid safe rollback when multiple nodes rejoin; telemetry hooks: new metrics slo.softfall.resume_attempts, slo.softfall.thaw_tokens, and slo.softfall.reject_rate with trace tags for tenant and circuit_epoch. The change is intentionally conservative: default behavior is off for tenants without historical throttling, and a runtime flag redwood.slo.softfall.enabled controls rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Implement orchestration controller and safe defaults - [x] Soft resume proxy w/ pace trimmer - [x] Telemetry and dashboards (new Grafana panels pointing to slo.softfall.*) - [x] Unit tests for thaw allocator and proxy decision logic - [x] Integration test in perf-canary with a synthetic reconnect storm - [x] Documentation note in runtime/operational-playbooks (brief)

Backwards compatibility and rollout: Defaults are conservative; feature gated via runtime flag and rollout is staged by canary->region rollout. No API surface changes. The change touches control-plane orchestration and runtime proxy; we coordinated a short maintenance window for early adopter Dedicated customers.

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of global valve-based shedding we implement per-tenant soft-thaw budgeting combined with a connection pacing layer to avoid synchronized reopen storms. This allows us to preserve SLOs for healthy tenants while gradually reinstating capacity for previously-quarantined tenants.

Follow-ups planned: expose a per-tenant thaw override for client support, add an adaptive decay based on successful token consumption, and integrate with the SLO enforcer state machine to allow prioritized thawing for high-tier customers.

review_comments: Anika Rao: Can we ensure thaw tokens cannot be accumulated indefinitely? Suggest adding a max window and decay — addressed by adding a sliding expiry to tokens (see thaw_allocator.go).

Jonas Peters: Pace trimming looks good but edge-case: mobile clients with poor RTT may starve. Added an expedite flag and client-class heuristic to allow small immediate bursts for mobile tier — documented.
Lena Ortiz: Add telemetry tags for circuit_epoch and tenant_tier so we can correlate restarts with KV pressure spikes — implemented.
Marco Bellini (author): Responded to all comments, added tests for token expiry and mobile expedite, and re-ran canary per reviewers' suggestions.
ci_checks: integration (perf-canary): pass (stable under simulated restart storm)
release_notes: Hotfix: Introduce SoftFall resume safeguard and per-tenant gradual thaw to prevent synchronized post-quarantine reconnect storms. Default disabled; gated rollout. Adds telemetry metrics and dashboards.
notes_for_oncall: If acceptance tests show elevated softfall.thaw_tokens exhaustion (metric > 0.9 for >5m) consider increasing default token refill or temporarily toggling redwood.slo.softfall.enabled=false. In severe KV pressure cases, fall back to region-level shed via existing circuit policies.
post_merge_actions: 1) Roll out to perf-canary and monitor slo.softfall.reject_rate and slo.softfall.thaw_tokens. 2) After 24h, enable in one region with conservative defaults. 3) Follow-up PR to add per-tenant override UI in Console.
